## TL;DR
A handoff record stuck at "running" no longer outlives its check. Records not backed by a live process, or older than a newer review verdict or status change, are cleared or reported as stale, and the task card, drawer and CLI show the real state. Move to done is no longer disabled by a stale record when the task is landable.

## Work and rationale
`handoff-status` reconciles a `running` record against live handoff and check processes, the task's current status and the latest review pass, and reports `superseded` or `stale` when nothing backs it. The stale flag reaches every checks renderer (task card, pipeline view, drawer, checks progress display), and the task watchdog no longer writes to held tasks. Post-handoff checkpoint recovery ignores a crash-orphaned `gate` marker. Review 3 found two defects, both fixed: the startup sweep deleted `review`-phase markers (a pending delta review owns them, and close-out resumes from them), now only `gate` markers are swept; and a second Move to done during a running delta review cleared the marker and restarted the gate, now it is refused while the review runs. Tests cover both, plus a stale record with a newer review pass and with no live process.

## Approaches tried
Reconciling in each renderer separately, then one server-side reconcile that every consumer reads, then scoping marker cleanup to the phase a handoff process actually backs.

## Challenges and blockers
Three review rounds, each finding a narrow lifecycle edge of the same class (which markers a live process backs). The first handoffs also failed on a consumed report draft.

## Key learnings
Cleanup of persisted state must be scoped to the phase that a live process owns. Reconcile derived state once on the server so every renderer agrees.
